headline: Math is nearly solved while agents doing real work remain the bottleneck
outlook: Math is the clearest story: models closed 95% of the remaining headroom there over the past year, FrontierMath passed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has now posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work closed just 34%, the least of any area. A burst of APEX-Agents records has pushed that benchmark to 82.2% with Gemini 4 Argon, but OSWorld 2 sits at 31.4% and the Remote Labor Index at 20.8%, and on current trends neither reaches 90% before mid-2027 and early 2028 respectively. The length of tasks models can handle points the other way: it is at 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview and doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends puts a full 40-hour work-week around December 2026, though the likely range stretches to August 2027. Meanwhile, the cheapest price for at least 80% on GPQA has fallen from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens and could dip under a cent in early 2027, so the coming year may be defined less by raw capability than by whether cheap, long-running agents translate into real work, keeping in mind that past forecast ranges caught the actual date only 59% of the time, with a typical miss of five months.
